Urban beekeeping has expanded considerably over the past decade, with rooftop hives appearing on offices, hotels and apartment buildings across many European capitals. Advocates argue that the practice raises public awareness of pollinator decline, although ecologists increasingly warn that densely packed honeybee colonies may compete with wild bee species for limited floral resources. Consequently, several municipalities have introduced registration schemes, requiring keepers to demonstrate adequate training and to justify the number of hives they maintain.
